description: JSON parameter wire form: the generated JSON type is written by exec, a batch of lone placeholders and a batch of rows and read back, and the stored document is described with the engine's own functions, compared with the same text as a literal and found by the document as a parameter; the document holds spacing, key order, a trailing zero, HTML characters and two- and four-byte UTF-8. ClickHouse's JSON type normalises a document. The database/sql emitter writes the document as text through sglClickHouseValue; it reads a JSON column through the JSON type's Scan, which encodes the driver's value again (HTML characters escaped). An Array(JSON) and a Tuple holding JSON are written too. Reads: clickhouse-go returns a JSON value inside an Array, a Map or a Tuple as its own chcol.JSON, which database/sql cannot store into the JSON type, so such columns read through the driver-composite scan adapter, in a one-row read, a stream, a UNION ALL whose second arm has a parameter of its own, an embed and a runtime builder, a Nullable(JSON) column, and inside Array(JSON), Array(Nullable(JSON)), Map(String, Nullable(JSON)), Map(String, Array(JSON)), a Map of named tuples, a named or unnamed Tuple and an Array and a Map of unnamed tuples, whose map[string]any or []any holds the JSON type. Every document reads as the same bytes as case 123 reads natively. A Map(String, JSON) column, which clickhouse-go panics returning through database/sql, is refused (Q059) and not read here.
